title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a case of a generative image tool used to alter a photograph of real, identifiable people and then published as if it were a record of them. The failure sits at the point of publication, not at the point of generation: the edit was made, and the altered image was placed on campus banners without anyone checking it against the original or against the university's own rules. The university has said the alteration and the failure to disclose it both violated a policy that prohibits using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people and events.

The failure mode is a system used outside the conditions it was built for, and a deployment without a human check. An image model asked to change who appears in a photo will produce a plausible image, and plausibility is exactly what makes the output hard to catch by eye. Catching it would have required a review step that compared the published image to the source photo and a disclosure that the image had been altered. Neither happened before the banners went up.

What is not established is who inside Residential and Dining Enterprises made or approved the edit, what tool was used, and whether anyone intended the specific substitution. The reports describe an acknowledged policy violation, not a finding of intent.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
Stanford University used artificial intelligence to alter a 2024 photo of students at a Lunar New Year party. In the original image, posted by the university's dining service, Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology, appeared with two other students. When Stanford reused the photo on campus banners last week, Ramirez had been replaced by a Black woman, and the other students had been made to look thinner. Ramirez learned about the change from a friend and said he found it upsetting, though he also saw a comedic element to it.

Stanford acknowledged on Tuesday that it had used artificial intelligence to change the image. The university said its policy strictly prohibits using A.I. to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities or achievements, and that both the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Stanford said it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide additional training and to ensure proper review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
